You have more completed work than the old plans suggest

This repository contains a working local runner, a substantial separate Starlark lab, a graphical-app translator, and several finished experiments. It also contains many dated plans that were never updated after implementation. Reading those plans alone makes the project look much more unfinished than it is.

My assessment is that the clearest problem is status drift: the documents disagree about what is current. There is also real expansion in optional tools, integration routes, and proposed research. That expansion is useful to make visible, but I cannot prove that it is all unwanted “scope creep.” Scope creep means work grows beyond its agreed purpose without a clear new decision. Only you can decide which directions still serve your purpose.

These numbers count records, not active projects.

The CSV has 327 rows: 15 parent programs and 312 detailed records. A finding, a phase, and its parent can describe the same underlying work. Do not add parent and child counts into a task total or turn these categories into a completion percentage.

The most actionable unfinished work is concentrated: a reviewed-but-unlanded Starlark recovery branch, an open path-safety fix, some native coordinator correctness gaps, and a packaged T3 live acceptance check. Datadog, Jev, most Shortcut recipes, and many architecture ideas remain proposals or later choices.

What I checked, and what I can actually know

I checked the real repository, its tracked plans, handoffs, roadmaps, current implementation, tests, Git history, registered working folders, and live GitHub branch/pull-request metadata. I swept 220 current tracked document files and read the focused Starlark README, and consulted two removed historical documents plus four branch-only handoff files. Markdown and HTML companions count as separate files. The source appendix identifies every file in that sweep.

The source sweep was broad; depth varied. Planning/status documents and important contradictory claims received focused reading and source tracing. Ordinary setup/reference material was scanned for direction and status. This is not a claim that every line of every source file or every historical conversation was reviewed.

I read historical Claude/Cursor reports as project evidence. I did not consult either agent’s new independent audit, and I did not contact them. This report is my independent assessment, not a four-person agreement.

Repository evidence cannot recover every “yes” from every conversation.

Each record distinguishes an explicit owner decision, recorded implementation with no original approval transcript, and a suggestion whose approval is not established. A proposal is not a promise. “Unknown” means evidence is insufficient, not that the work never happened.

I excluded private runner/session payloads, credential values, raw live-run prompts and logs, unrelated vendored catalog bodies, and the separate Codex sibling’s implementation. No paid model calls, account changes, app setting changes, merges, stash restores, or document cleanup were performed.

Date interpretation: first_recorded_date is the earliest located scoped evidence used here, not a certified date of inception or your first approval. latest_evidence_date records the evidence date or this audit inspection; it does not mean the code changed that day. Confidence describes how strongly the status is supported, not how well the feature works.

Publication: GitHub identifies this repository as public. “nsfw” is your folder convention; it does not provide access control. These sanitized reports will be public when pushed, as requested. Your independent-review arrangement relies on Claude and Cursor respecting your instruction not to peek.

The different directions are separate pieces

Ordinary runner route

Your prompt → native runner → local bridge → Claude → a proposed tool action → the runner checks permission → the local action runs.

The bridge is the connection. The runner is the loop deciding what happens next. They are related, but changing one does not automatically fix the other.

Graphical-app route

T3 app → ACP translator → the same native runner → the bridge.

ACP means Agent Client Protocol: a shared message format that lets an app talk to an agent. The translator is built; the newest packaged-app acceptance checklist is still incomplete.

Separate Starlark lab

A planner describes a bounded workflow → Starlark evaluator checks/runs its plan → the host starts workers → results can be combined and recovered.

Starlark is a small programming language used to describe work. This is intentionally a separate lab. The owner-approved R8 decision keeps it out of the normal runner’s tool list.

Optional measurements and convenience

Datadog dashboards, Jev ranking/classification, Mac Shortcuts, container environments, and benchmark campaigns sit around those core paths.

A written guide or recipe is evidence of an idea being explored. It is not proof that the service, app, or automation was installed and tested.

The native coordinator and Starlark coordinator are also separate. A coordinator is code that starts several jobs and combines results. Starlark’s durable campaign accounting does not automatically solve the native coordinator’s cache/budget or verification gaps.

How the directions accumulated

April–May: bridge transport began; the local runner appeared; performance/caching and harness plans grew around it. Compatibility surfaces were later deliberately removed.

June–early July: optional tools, child agents, hooks, memory, worktrees, Mac recipes, and a separate Codex-fork direction broadened the experiments.

Mid–late July: attention shifted to matching promises with behavior: runtime concordance, permission safaris, context rebuilding, and making tests detect ineffective protection.

Late July–August: orchestration studies turned into bounded prototypes. Starlark moved under Git; its budgeting, worker contracts, evaluation, and recovery grew. ACP/T3 became another way to use the runner.

Late August–September: context history recovery, terminal-state evaluation, protocol cancellation, bridge hosting, command-builder consistency, and Starlark interruption recovery received focused work.

Today: many old “not started” labels are obsolete. Two code-bearing objectives still live outside main; several later acceptance checks and review findings remain open; most remaining research expansion is optional.

My feedback: make decisions smaller before making the project smaller

I would keep the native runner as the everyday learning surface, preserve Starlark as its separate research lab, and avoid adding another integration route until the current evidence gaps are understood. That is a recommendation for your consideration, not a decision I have made for you.

Order Decision / direction Concrete scope Pros and tradeoff Evidence
1 Close existing evidence gaps before expanding Review Starlark branch S-03; refresh/review the narrow HS-01 fix; decide whether to finish the packaged T3 acceptance check. Makes existing work trustworthy and gives a clear stop point. It delays new experimentation while reviews/checks happen. S-03 · HS-01 · ACP-LIVE
2 Resolve native correctness before more orchestration Prioritize success gating, failed-worker admission, managed-worktree composition and recovery health. Cache-aware budgets matter if you use native parallel jobs. Targets real composition gaps. It is several independent slices; avoid authorizing an all-at-once rewrite. ARCH-01 · ARCH-03 · ARCH-04 · A1-F5 · A3-F4
3 Keep the next optional experiment singular Choose at most one among Jev shadow evaluation, Datadog adapter, a real Shortcut, or a new model comparison. Define one question and one evidence-producing stop point. Preserves curiosity with an understandable result. Choosing one means consciously parking other possibilities. JEV · OBS-02 · MAC-01 · S-05
4 Normalize status after the independent audits Compare contradictory rows by stable ID, then agree what is current, parked, and superseded. Preserve historical documents and add pointers in a separately authorized pass. Reduces confusion without erasing history. It requires resolving disagreements first; a bulk document cleanup would be premature. D-02 · D-11 · D-09

You do not need to choose a new overall roadmap today. First compare our three independent inventories. Then you can say “keep,” “park,” or “stop” for a parent program, and authorize one bounded next task. A completed experiment may simply stay completed.

One private confirmation remains separate from project planning.

An August 10 architecture report recorded a credential exposure in reachable Git history. It also recorded current-file cleanup. I did not retrieve or reproduce the value, and I found no repository record proving rotation/revocation. You can confirm containment privately; this audit does not rewrite history or treat the historical report as proof that a currently valid secret remains exposed. See ARCH-10.

Status vocabulary

Status Detailed records What it means
Implemented 126 The narrow component exists in current main. Read its limits; existence and automated tests do not prove every live use.
Experiment concluded 19 The recorded question was investigated and a scoped result was written. There is no automatic next build commitment.
Retired 23 Removed, superseded, or explicitly outside the chosen direction. Preserve its history; do not restart it from an old checkbox.
Partial 63 Something real exists, with a located gap, incomplete acceptance, or missing integration.
Branch only 2 A fix exists on another Git branch and has not joined main. Main does not inherit it.
Deferred 24 Explicitly parked or a named later phase that has not been undertaken.
Proposed 47 A recommendation, recipe, or design exists; implementation or owner approval is not established.
Unknown 8 The available evidence cannot support a more definite status, or implementation belongs outside the audited repository.

How to use the files

Open this HTML report in a browser, such as Safari or Chrome. You can search and filter the embedded records. You do not need Terminal for that. Open the CSV with Numbers or Excel: in Finder, select the CSV, right-click, choose “Open With,” then choose the spreadsheet app. Success looks like one header row and 327 data rows spread across 23 columns. If everything appears in one column, use the app’s import settings and select comma as the separator and UTF-8 as the text encoding.

The CSV is the comparison data. The Alan report explains it. Give the agent-facing HTML and CSV to Claude and Cursor only after each finishes its independent audit, as you planned. Local evidence links assume the reports stay in this repository folder; moving the HTML alone leaves those links without their source files.

To save a full PDF in your browser, use Print → Save as PDF. The report opens evidence panels before printing. Reset filters first if you want every record included.

A small glossary

Word Plain-language meaning
Repository The project’s saved files and their recorded history.
Git The tool that records snapshots of file changes.
Commit One recorded snapshot, identified by a long hexadecimal label.
Branch A named line of snapshots; work on another branch is not automatically in main.
main The repository’s ordinary shared line of work.
Worktree A separate local folder attached to a branch or snapshot of the same repository.
Push / sync Send local commits to GitHub; here, verify local main and GitHub main identify the same snapshot.
Pull request A GitHub request to merge a branch into another branch. An open request is not a completed merge.
Runtime The code path that actually runs during use, rather than a helper that only has isolated tests.
Capability An explicitly enabled group of tools, such as file edits.
Shell The command-running program that can act with your Mac account’s authority.
JSON / JSONL / NDJSON JavaScript Object Notation is a structured text format; JSON Lines and newline-delimited JSON put one record on each line.
JSON-RPC JSON Remote Procedure Call: a request/response message format using structured JSON text.
HTTP / HTTPS Hypertext Transfer Protocol is a software/web request format; HTTPS adds an encrypted connection.
LSP / MCP / SDK Language Server Protocol provides code intelligence; Model Context Protocol connects tools; a software development kit is a library for building with a service.
UI / UX User interface is what you see and operate; user experience is how understandable and usable that interaction feels.
UTF-8 / byte-order marker UTF-8 is the text encoding used here; a small leading marker helps spreadsheet apps recognize it correctly.
Signal / SIGTERM / SIGKILL An operating-system message to a process. Termination signal can allow cleanup; kill signal immediately stops it.
Cache / token A cache reuses earlier work. A token is a small unit of text used to measure model input/output.
SLO / APM / telemetry Service-level objective is a chosen reliability target; application performance monitoring measures timed operations; telemetry is recorded measurement data.
API key / fingerprint An API key is a secret access credential. Here a fingerprint is a saved client-request identity/shape, which can also contain sensitive account details.
Kernel / stub / adapter Kernel here means the wrapper around the agent loop; a stub is a limited placeholder; an adapter translates one component’s interface to another.
Node.js / Go Programming runtimes/toolchains used by this repository: Node.js runs JavaScript, and Go compiles the Starlark evaluator.
HTML / PDF Hypertext Markup Language is the browser document format; Portable Document Format is the printable document format.
Ledger / receipt A written record of events or a received response used to understand recovery/accounting.
Durable Saved so selected state survives interruption; the exact failure boundary still matters.
Invariant A rule that should remain true across all supported paths.
Golden test / false green A golden test compares known expected outcomes; a false green is a test reporting success despite ineffective behavior.
CI Continuous integration: automated checks triggered by repository activity.
CSV Comma-separated values: a plain-text spreadsheet format.
TODO An explicitly recorded known test gap, not a successful assertion.
OAuth A login authorization method that lets the bridge use existing account authorization without copying a normal API key.
ACP / API / CLI Agent Client Protocol is the app/agent message format; application programming interface is a software entry point; command-line interface is a program controlled by typed commands.
